solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Street split in old-fashioned struggle

blocks.note: ST is the standard abbreviation for street
a rift is a split or crack

explanation.surface: A road divided by an old-style fight between neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: STRIFT is an archaic form of strife, hence 'old-fashioned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Strift is an obsolete variant of strife, meaning conflict or contention.

clue.text: Onset of rime, as in April alas, bad for plant

indicators.note: an onset is a beginning, so only the opening letter is kept
in places the selected letter among the letters that follow
bad suggests the letters are spoiled and out of order

blocks.note: the first letter of rime
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Frost arriving in spring, as in a cold April, is bad news for gardeners.
explanation.walkthrough: Rime is hoar frost; its first letter joins the letters of 'as April alas' and the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarsaparilla is a tropical climbing plant whose root flavours a soft drink.

clue.text: Bad guy with nasty scar, US gangster

indicators.note: nasty implies something twisted and disagreeable, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters rearranged
Al Capone, the notorious Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A villain bearing an ugly scar, an American mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a scoundrel or rogue, a dishonest person.

clue.text: Hat for dame going out, not maiden

indicators.note: going out suggests things breaking up and scattering, so the letters are rearranged
not tells us a letter is to be excluded

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Headwear for a lady going out, who is no longer a young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The M is removed from 'for dame' before the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown.

clue.text: Vehicle trade on the upturn

indicators.note: in a down clue an upturn sends the word upward, reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: a mart is a market, a place of trade

explanation.surface: Business in vehicles is improving.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a passenger vehicle running on rails in the street.

clue.text: Devilish type, individual set up by authority?

blocks.note: an imp is a little devil
one, as in a single individual

explanation.surface: A mischievous person installed in a post by those in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: IMPONE is an old word meaning to impose, so something imponed is laid down by authority; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To impone is an archaic verb for impose, establishing something by decree.

clue.text: Nibbles for Scots politicians — two eggs consumed

indicators.note: something consumed is taken inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: MPs are Members of Parliament
an egg is shaped like O, so two give two Os

explanation.surface: Scottish MPs snack on a couple of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To moop is a Scots verb meaning to nibble or munch.

clue.text: Locating green activity

blocks.note: first meaning: placing, setting down
second meaning: what golfers do on the green, pronounced differently

explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' suggests environmentalism but is the golf green; the two senses are spelt alike and said differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the participle of put, meaning placing, and also the golf stroke that rolls the ball toward the hole.

clue.text: Bony couple of ducks eating grubs finally

indicators.note: eating takes food inside, so one piece goes within another
finally points to the very end of the word, its last letter

blocks.note: the first of the couple: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
the last letter of grubs
the second of the couple: the teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: Two scrawny ducks feeding on larvae at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The couple is two different kinds of duck: O, the cricketer's zero, and TEAL, the bird. The S goes inside the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal means relating to or resembling bone, from the Greek for bone.

clue.text: Stop put to bad feeling — intended to eliminate a threat to safety

indicators.note: eliminate means remove, so a letter is taken out of the preceding word

blocks.note: to end is to stop
anger is a bad feeling
meant means intended
taken as written

explanation.surface: An end is put to resentment, a bid to remove a hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: Endangerment is the act of putting someone or something at risk.

clue.text: Curse action hatched up by intimate friend no longer

indicators.note: a plot hatched up is contrived or cooked up, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan to put a curse on someone, cooked up by a former close friend.
explanation.walkthrough: A catercousin is an archaic term, hence 'no longer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Catercousin is an obsolete word for a bosom companion or close intimate.

clue.text: More old-fashioned India in trouble

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
being in a corner is being in a tight spot or trouble

explanation.surface: A rather dated India finds itself in difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Corny means trite or dated, so the comparative is more hackneyed.

clue.text: Possibly slam old F1 driver losing power?

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter drops out of the named driver

blocks.note: Alain Prost, four-time Formula One world champion
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Might someone criticise a retired racing driver who has lost his engine power?
explanation.walkthrough: ROST is an old form of roast, and to roast someone is to slam them; 'Possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Rost is an obsolete spelling of roast, which in its slang sense means criticise severely.

clue.text: Call to politician to make progress in tricky conditions?

blocks.note: yo is a call or greeting
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Phoning a politician to ask them to push on through difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: YOMP is British military slang for marching with heavy kit over rough terrain, made famous in the Falklands.
explanation.definitionFit: To yomp is to march laboriously across difficult ground carrying a heavy pack.

clue.text: Oil wheels that have got dry inside

indicators.note: the wheels have got something within them, so they hold it
inside confirms the middle piece sits within the outer ones

blocks.note: a wheel is round like the letter O
TT, teetotal, means dry
the second wheel, another O

explanation.surface: Lubricant for wheels that have dried out on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheels' is plural, giving two Os, with TT (teetotal, so dry) between them. 'Inside' completes the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a variant of attar, the fragrant oil distilled from rose petals.

clue.text: Insects troubled a mother going about work

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so its letters are thrown out of order
going about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap round another piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Bugs bother a busy mother while she goes about her job.
explanation.definitionFit: Homoptera is an order of insects including aphids, cicadas and leafhoppers.

clue.text: The one for me could be a ragman!

definitions.text: The one for me could be a ragman!

indicators.note: could be suggests one possible arrangement of letters among many

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a rag-and-bone man could be their ideal partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue speaks as the answer: 'a ragman' is a rearrangement of its letters, so the clue is itself an instance of the device it names.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by reordering another's letters is this kind of wordplay, and the clue's own fodder is exactly such a reordering.

clue.text: Allow ancient worker maybe to hold gathering up

indicators.note: to hold something is to contain it, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a worker bee; 'maybe' flags it as one example
a meet is a gathering, as of a hunt

explanation.surface: Let an old labourer hold a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' belongs with 'Allow': BETEEME is a Spenserian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Beteem is an archaic verb, used by Shakespeare and Spenser, meaning to permit or grant.

clue.text: Tiresome person presented with gold dish

blocks.note: a pill is slang for a tedious person
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A bore is handed a golden platter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillau is a variant spelling of pilaf, a spiced rice dish.

clue.text: In song archdeacon becomes animated

indicators.note: In places the following piece within the one named first

blocks.note: a lied is a German art song
Ven, Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A churchman comes to life when singing.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: Livened means made lively, cheered up or animated.

clue.text: Move nimbly around on wooden support

indicators.note: turned around, the word for darting quickly runs the other way

blocks.note: to nip is to move quickly and nimbly
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: Someone skipping about cleverly despite a wooden leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' and 'leg' are interchangeable cricket terms for the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinleg is a wooden leg, an artificial limb supporting the wearer.

clue.text: Roman official wants a food item with no hint of burning

indicators.note: no hint of means the opening letter of the following word is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
an edible is something fit to eat
the first letter of burning

explanation.surface: A Roman magistrate fancies some food that has not been charred.
explanation.definitionFit: An aedile was a magistrate in ancient Rome responsible for public buildings and games.

clue.text: Shrine with a bulge, notice, being erected

indicators.note: something erected is put upright, so in a down clue the letters read upward

blocks.note: taken as written
to bag is to bulge or hang loosely
an ad is a notice

explanation.surface: A shrine with a swelling and a sign being put up beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dagaba is a Buddhist dome-shaped shrine for relics, a stupa.

clue.text: Not all love musical birds

indicators.note: not all means only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters span the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Not everyone enjoys birds that sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless Australian birds.

clue.text: Component of building — a terrific entrance

indicators.note: a component is a part, so the answer is a part of the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word, the next word and the start of another

explanation.surface: Praise for a part of a building: a grand doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'building' look like a definition, but it holds the start of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingate is an entrance or inlet, such as the channel into a mould.

clue.text: Led by eccentric aunt, children dance

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, out of the ordinary, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters rearranged
CH is a common abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: Children follow their quirky aunt in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Led by' sets the order: the rearranged aunt comes before the children.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautch is a traditional Indian dance performed by professional dancing girls.

clue.text: What would be crazy entering zone with English coming out?

definitions.text: What would be crazy entering zone with English coming out?

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece goes into another
coming out means leaving, so the letter departs from the build

blocks.note: mad means crazy
an area is a zone
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A riddle about a mad incursion into English waters, with the English sailing out to meet it.
explanation.walkthrough: MAD goes into AREA and the E leaves. Read whole, the clue describes the Spanish fleet of 1588: a crazy venture entering English waters, met by the English fleet coming out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish Armada was a reckless invading fleet that entered the Channel as English ships sailed out to fight it.

clue.text: Animal god of Hinduism losing tail, gaining one

indicators.note: losing the end and gaining something means the last letter is swapped for a new one

blocks.note: Indra is the Hindu god of thunder and rain
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A beast sacred to a Hindu deity has lost its tail and gained something else.
explanation.definitionFit: The indri is a large lemur of Madagascar.

clue.text: Thinner mister, bore for entertainment

indicators.note: a host entertains guests by taking them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Mr is the abbreviation for mister
an eagre is a tidal bore, a surge up a river

explanation.surface: A skinnier man has a dull guest to amuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' is not a tedious person but a tidal wave in a river, for which EAGRE is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means lean or scanty, so the comparative is more lean.

clue.text: University for one clever and innocent

indicators.note: one thing for another means it takes the other's place

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
I is the Roman numeral one
ingenious means clever and inventive

explanation.surface: A university student who is both bright and naive.
explanation.walkthrough: U replaces the I (one) in INGENIOUS to give INGENUOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenuous means artless, frank and unsuspecting, much like naive.

clue.text: Neglect of old university in America

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: The decline of a historic American college.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to leave out or fail to do, which is to neglect.

clue.text: Sign of appreciation for bananas?

blocks.note: first meaning: a round of applause, as in 'give them a big one'
second meaning: a bunch of bananas growing together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' suggests madness, but it is the fruit, whose clusters have a special name.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause is called a big one of these, and a cluster of bananas is also known by the same word.

clue.text: Thin plate is weak

blocks.note: first meaning: a thin metal plate, as in armour
second meaning: feeble, unconvincing

explanation.walkthrough: As a noun this is one of the overlapping strips in a suit of armour; as an adjective, as in a feeble excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a strip of armour plating and also describes a poor, unconvincing effort.

clue.text: I recited Bible. not the first or last sadly to be destroyer of freedom

indicators.note: dropping first and last means trimming both ends off the preceding word
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written
the word with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: Reciting scripture badly turns someone into an enemy of liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberticide is one who destroys liberty, by analogy with words like regicide.

clue.text: A son of Jacob in charge of Jewish tradition

blocks.note: taken as written
Gad was one of the twelve sons of Jacob
IC is short for in charge

explanation.surface: One of Jacob's sons took charge of Jewish custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadic means relating to the Aggadah, the non-legal narrative tradition of rabbinic literature.

clue.text: Stop that conflict knocking out America

indicators.note: one thing knocking out another drives it from its place and takes over its spot

blocks.note: taken as written
war is armed conflict
A is an abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: An appeal to halt a war that removes the United States from combat.
explanation.walkthrough: A whole word replaces a single letter here: the conflict knocks the America abbreviation out of 'that' and sits where it stood.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart is to stop or frustrate someone's plans.
